message: Tool input reaches a dangerous call: a file is written / deleted / moved at a path taken from tool input.
fix: Optional hardening: use fs.mkdtempSync and write with flag 'wx' / mode 0o600.
source_quote: export async function importTmx(args: any, lara: Translator) {
reason: The path is built entirely by the server (fixed temp directory + timestamp + random suffix); only the file content (tmx_content, capped at 5MB) comes from the tool arguments, and the file is deleted in finally. No attacker control over where it is written.

title: HTTP transport binds 0.0.0.0 by default with wildcard CORS

evidence.quote: // Bind specifically on 127.0.0.1 to avoid binding to all interfaces

reason: Contrary to the comment, the HTTP server listens on all interfaces by default and cors() without an origin option answers any Origin; impact is limited because every /mcp request must carry the caller's own Lara keys (no server-held credential), so it mainly exposes a free relay and the debug logs.
fix: Default HOST to 127.0.0.1 (set 0.0.0.0 only in the Docker env), set an explicit CORS origin allowlist and validate Origin/Host on /mcp.

title: delete_memory / delete_translation delete account data with no confirmation

evidence.quote: export async function deleteMemory(args: any, lara: Translator) {

reason: A prompt injection in any text the agent is translating can make it call list_memories then delete_memory on every id, permanently destroying the user's translation memories; there is no confirmation, dry-run or destructive hint.
fix: Mark these tools destructiveHint: true so clients ask for approval, require an explicit confirm argument matching the memory name, or move deletes out of the MCP tool set.

title: Debug logging writes full MCP request bodies and the access key id

evidence.quote: logger.debug("Creating MCP server with credentials: " + accessKeyId);

reason: sanitizeBody only redacts top-level keys, so at debug level every tool call's arguments (texts being translated, TMX content) and responses are logged, together with each caller's Lara access key id; the secret itself is redacted.
fix: Do not log JSON-RPC params/results or key ids; log method name and tool name only.
